newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity falls after cautious FT comment.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity falls after cautious FT comment.

text.p: Shares in LucasVarity Plc fell on Wednesday as investors took a more sober view of this week's trading statement and the "Lex" column in the Financial Times said it was hard to see the shares outperforming.
LucasVarity shares were down 10-1/2p at 209-1/2 by 1454 GMT, erasing gains made on Tuesday when the firm's trading statement was released.
"The shares did well yesterday and people seem to be concluding today that it was maybe overdone," one market-maker said.

LucasVarity's trading statement said it would not cut its dividend without also launching a share buy-back. But the Financial Times said tax issues made a buy-back a less effective means of returning cash to shareholders.

"A recent change in UK taxation rules means that a share buy-back is now less tax-efficient for pension funds than dividends," it said. "So overall, a buy-back wastes value which a special dividend would not."
The newspaper said the rest of the company's trading statement also failed to provide much comfort.

"The bulk of the 120 million stg of promised merger cost savings will not impact until 1998 and market conditions remain tough. Despite yesterday's bounce, it is hard to see the shares outperforming," it said.
